{{Short description|Mathematical technique used in environmental sciences}}
[[File:RSS troposphere stratosphere trend.png|thumb|Worldwide temperature trend analysis]]'''Trend surface analysis''', also known as '''trend surface mapping''', is a mathematical technique used in [[archaeology]] and [[environmental science]]s such as [[geology]] and [[soil science]]. The method involves using low-order [[polynomial]]s of spatial coordinates to estimate a regular grid of points from scattered observations such as archeological finds or [[soil survey]] results.<ref>{{Citation |last=Agterberg |first=Frits P. |chapter=Trend Surface Analysis |date=1984 |title=Spatial Statistics and Models |pages=147–171 |editor-last=Gaile |editor-first=Gary L. |chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-94-017-3048-8_8 |access-date=2024-04-20 |place=Dordrecht |publisher=Springer Netherlands |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-94-017-3048-8_8 |isbn=978-90-481-8385-2 |editor2-last=Willmott |editor2-first=Cort J.|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>
